title: Reduce GPU working set via temporal activation coalescing and fusion-aware allocator
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Large sequence workloads frequently create transient activation lifetimes that overlap only briefly across batches. The runtime's current allocator and kernel scheduling treat these activations independently which increases peak device working set. This PR introduces a temporal activation coalescer that identifies short-lived activation groups across overlapping microbatches and co-allocates them into compact regions, combined with a lightweight fusion-aware allocator that prefers contiguous allocations for kernels that will be fused in the JIT path.

Changes (high level):
- Temporal activation coalescer: a pass in the request planner that tracks activation live ranges across continuous batching windows and emits coalescing hints to the allocator. The algorithm is conservative (no reordering) and operates on live-range summaries to keep overhead <1% CPU.
- Fusion-aware allocator: allocator modifications to prefer contiguous spans for allocations tagged with fuse-hint; falls back to existing allocation strategy when fragmentation risk is high.
- KV cache coalescer: small heuristic that groups stale KV shards that have identical eviction scores into a single slab to reduce per-shard metadata and transient workspace.
- Microbatch scheduler tweak: when temporal coalescing is enabled, the continuous batching scheduler exposes a slight delay (configurable, default 1ms) to increase overlap opportunity between adjacent microbatches. This trades negligible latency for lower peak memory in tail-heavy workloads.
- Telemetry and safety: added per-request histogram metrics for coalesce-hit, coalesce-size, and a safety guard which rejects coalescing when available workspace < 5% of capacity.

Why this is different: prior efforts reduced scratch via arena tuning and checkpointing; this PR reduces peak working set by exploiting temporal overlap and kernel-fusion locality without changing model checkpoints or introducing new spill paths. It targets production workloads that run many small concurrent streams with continuous batching enabled.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed with infra and runtime teams
- [x] Unit tests for allocator heuristics
- [x] End-to-end perf job run against long-tail translation workload
- [x] Telemetry hooks added to Console dashboards (follow-up PR wires visuals)

Performance summary (from perf run):
- 95th-percentile GPU memory usage reduced by ~18% on long-tail translation test (batching window 20ms).
- Average per-token latency increased by +0.4% (within SLO) when default 1ms coalesce delay is enabled; configuration allows disabling the delay per route.
- Cost per token estimate reduced by ~12% after normalization for throughput gains.

Related: references ENG-1289 (working-set analysis) and ENG-1301 (continuous batching improvements).

file_snippets:
// fusion_allocator.cc: prefer contiguous runs for fuse-hint allocations
if (meta.fuse_hint && try_contiguous_run(size, &run)) { allocate_run(run); } else { fallback_alloc(size); }

// temporal_coalescer.cc: summarize live ranges per microbatch window
for (auto &r : request.live_ranges) { summary.merge(r); }
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This looks promising; can you quantify CPU overhead of the coalescer on p95 request rate?
Maya Patel: Measured ~0.6% CPU at p95 on our perf harness (added to description). I tuned the summarization to be O(n) over live ranges.
Rina Sato: Please add a safety gate when GPUs are under memory pressure so we don't end up making allocation decisions that lead to OOMs.
Maya Patel: Added safety guard: coalescing disabled when free workspace < 5% and added test coverage.
Diego Marquez: Approve after minor test naming nit; no behavioral concerns from me.
CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, lint).
tests_and_ci_notes: Unit tests added for allocator heuristics and KV coalescer. Integration perf runs executed in perf-lab (stable infra); CI flake isolated to metrics ingestion test and fixed in follow-up commit.
release_notes: Reduced GPU peak working set for continuous-batching workloads via temporal activation coalescing and fusion-aware allocations. This can improve throughput and reduce per-token cost at small latency trade-offs; controllable via runtime config.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.temporal_coalesce=false by default on older clusters. Ops teams should enable on representative canary nodes and monitor coalesce-hit and coalesce-size histograms before rolling to fleets.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect coalescing could increase fragmentation or cause transient OOMs. Mitigation: conservative heuristics, safety gate when workspace <5%, and ability to disable per-route. Extensive unit tests and a staged rollout plan were used.
